reuse.why: Reuses findOrCreateBank, syncAccount and handleSyncResponse, and puts the new guards in link.ts, but the takeover re-writes unlinkAccount's field reset instead of sharing it, and Fintegra copies an existing provider's link and download bodies.

duplication.why: linkFintegraAccount is a near-verbatim copy of linkSimpleFinAccount, downloadFintegraTransactions copies downloadAkahuTransactions, the unlink column reset is copied from unlinkAccount, and the open/not-linked guard pair is pasted into all six handlers.

placement.why: Guards live in accounts/link.ts next to findOrCreateBank, which fits, but an 'assert' function now performs the takeover write (unlinking another account), hiding a mutation inside a validation helper.

scope.why: All edits serve the four requests (one-link rule, Fintegra, closed-account refusal, takeover flag) with no unrelated churn.

maintainability.why: Every provider handler must remember to call two guards in the right order with an upgradingId check, assertAccountIsNotLinked silently mutates when given a boolean flag, and the unlink reset can drift from unlinkAccount.

bypasses_abstraction.where: assertAccountIsNotLinked in link.ts clears account_id/bank/balances/sync source with its own db.updateAccount instead of going through the existing unlinkAccount logic in app.ts

disguised_duplication.where: downloadFintegraTransactions and linkFintegraAccount are condensed/reformatted copies of downloadAkahuTransactions and linkSimpleFinAccount (merged lines, dropped intermediate variables) rather than shared code

abstraction_drift.where: assertAccountIsNotLinked (link.ts) gains the replaceExistingLink parameter and a branch that unlinks the holder instead of throwing; all six link handlers call it, each with its own preceding 'if (upgradingId) assertAccountIsOpen' block
